title: Burst elasticity scorecard memo
content:
Purpose:
This note collects a compact, human-readable scorecard comparing burst-handling elasticity across a small matrix of model variants and runtime knobs. Goal is to produce an operationally useful one-pager for product/solutions conversations: when customers ask "how much extra latency and $/token should we expect during a 10x microburst?" we can point to this artifact and an associated explainer.

Scope & constraints:
- Synthetic spike-driving workload: 60s warm period at baseline throughput (50 qps), then 60s microburst at 500 qps, then 120s cool-down.
- Models: small-medium-large open variants (S=1.3B, M=6B, L=34B) representative decode configs.
- Serving modes evaluated: fastpath (dedicated slots), multiplex (smallbatch), prefetch cache-on (kv-hit emulation), quantized runtime (4-bit int8-like path).
- Metrics: p50, p95 latency (ms) for last-token, and marginal $/1k tokens (inference-only compute cost estimate). Also report recovery time to p95 baseline.

Test matrix (short):
- S / M / L x modes: fastpath, multiplex, prefetch-on, quantized.
- Batch shapes: baseline steady (1–3 tok/session), burst sessions short (2–8 tok), long (20–60 tok).
- Network: colocated core region, no cross-region failover.

Raw (condensed) results table (text):
Columns: model | mode | p50_base | p95_base | p50_burst | p95_burst | recov_p95_s | $/1k_base | $/1k_burst
S | fastpath | 38 | 82 | 52 | 160 | 24s | 0.08 | 0.12
S | multiplex | 42 | 110 | 68 | 420 | 46s | 0.06 | 0.20
S | prefetch-on | 40 | 90 | 48 | 170 | 28s | 0.07 | 0.11
S | quantized | 36 | 78 | 50 | 200 | 30s | 0.05 | 0.14

M | fastpath | 72 | 160 | 98 | 420 | 32s | 0.20 | 0.36
M | multiplex | 84 | 230 | 140 | 820 | 78s | 0.16 | 0.62
M | prefetch-on | 76 | 170 | 90 | 380 | 36s | 0.18 | 0.31
M | quantized | 68 | 150 | 88 | 460 | 40s | 0.14 | 0.45

L | fastpath | 220 | 420 | 320 | 1220 | 40s | 0.92 | 2.60
L | multiplex | 260 | 610 | 420 | 2600 | 130s | 0.75 | 4.50
L | prefetch-on | 230 | 480 | 310 | 1150 | 42s | 0.85 | 2.40
L | quantized | 200 | 380 | 290 | 980 | 46s | 0.60 | 2.10

Notes on the table:
- p95_burst spikes are where the elastic behavior diverges most between modes. Multiplex suffers highest tail due to slot saturation and queueing amplification.
- Recovery time measured as elapsed seconds from burst end until p95 <= 1.2 * p95_base.
- $/1k estimates approximate GPU-cost-equivalents (amortized compute only). No networking or infra overheads included.

Scorecard methodology (one-line formulas):
- Latency shock = (p95_burst - p95_base) / p95_base (expressed as %).
- Cost shock = ($/1k_burst - $/1k_base) / $/1k_base (expressed as %).
- Composite burst stress score = 0.6 * normalized_latency_shock + 0.4 * normalized_cost_shock (normalize each metric to 0..1 across tested rows). Lower is better.

Compact score summary (ranked best->worst):
1) S / prefetch-on — consistently low p95 shock (~88%) and small cost shock, fastest recovery.
2) S / quantized — slightly lower cost baseline, modest tail amplification.
3) M / prefetch-on — acceptable for mid-tier, consider larger slot pool for spikes.
4) S / fastpath — good latency but higher cost delta under burst (reserved slots exhaust).
5) M / quantized — middling.
6) L / quantized — surprisingly competitive vs fastpath at tails due to smaller memory footprint per slot, but cost still large for sustained bursts.
7) M / multiplex — poor tail behavior, long recovery; not recommended for >5x bursts without admission control.
8) L / multiplex — worst; extreme tail and cost amplification.

Interpretation / trade-offs (informal):
- Prefetch-on (KV cache friendly) consistently smooths the p95 tail because common prefixes are compacted and work-stealing impact reduces queueing. This is especially high-value for small/medium models that see large request fanout during spikes.
- Multiplex (opportunistic batching) is cost-efficient during steady-state but amplifies tail under sudden high cardinality bursts due to contention on packing windows and global slot limits.
- Quantized runtimes reduce absolute compute cost and sometimes reduce p95_burst by shrinking per-session footprints (more concurrent sessions), but they can raise decoder latency variance in some model families — test per-model.
- For enterprise customers with bursty traffic (chat agents, concurrent queries), recommend hybrid: prefetch-on + reserved fastpath buffer that allows small number of warm slots to drain microbursts.

Recommended messaging for sales collateral (short bullets):
- "Burst-resilient patterns: enable prefetch, keep a small fastpath buffer, and consider quantization for predictable cost savings."
- Use a concrete example: "For a 10x short microburst on the M-class model, prefetch reduces p95 amplification by ~55% vs multiplex and cuts recovery time by ~50%."

Open questions / caveats:
- These runs were single-region, isolated hardware; cross-region failover and cold-warm mix could change recovery timings.
- Granularity of billing assumptions in $/1k needs legal/product validation (we used simple GPU-hour amortization).
- Longer bursts (minutes) trend results toward steady-state multiplex favorability; we did not model minute-scale saturation in this memo.

Action items (next steps):
- [ ] Run a follow-up with heterogeneous session lengths (mix heavy churn + long polling) — owner: Mateo. ETA: 2w.
- [ ] Add rack-level prefetch heatmap and include sample trace for a customer-facing slide — owner: Linnea. ETA: 1w.
- [ ] Confirm cost model with finance and the pricing team; replace $/1k with platform pricing buckets when approved — owner: Omar. ETA: 3w.

Notes-to-self: include ASCII sparkline for a microburst p95 timeline in the slide deck. Also, capture a brief snippet of a tail-caused error pattern (500/503) observed in multiplex runs — may be useful for SRE playbook.

Appendix (short):
- Test harness: open-source harness v0.9 (github link above), traffic generator seeded with Zipfian session arrival (skew=1.2).
- Hardware: A100-equivalent for L/M, V100-equivalent for S; normalization used FLOP-adjusted slot counts.
- Repro notes: raw traces under CONFLUENCE-PLAT-1243 > attachments > burst-run-2028-06-10.zip

End of memo.
summary: Compact benchmark scorecard comparing burst elasticity across small/medium/large model classes and runtime knobs (prefetch, multiplex, quantized, fastpath). Includes condensed result table, scoring method, interpretation, recommended customer messaging, open questions, and action items.
